subject: math
title: Positive and Negative Numbers: Real-World Meaning, Opposites and the Number Line
seo_title: Grade 6 Negative Numbers Worksheets: Integers in Real Life, Opposites and Number Lines (6.NS.C.5)
standard_text: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values (e.g., temperature above/below zero, elevation above/below sea level, credits/debits, positive/negative electric charge); use positive and negative numbers to represent quantities in real-world contexts, explaining the meaning of 0 in each situation.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 negative numbers worksheets: write positive and negative numbers for real-world situations, explain what 0 means, read integers, fractions and decimals on a number line, and find opposites like −(−5). 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Positive and negative numbers point in opposite directions from 0.
key_sub: Below zero, below sea level, a loss or a withdrawal is negative. Negative numbers are to the left of 0 on a number line, and opposites like 3 and −3 are the same distance from 0, so −(−3) = 3.
body_html:
Two directions from 0

Many quantities go in two opposite directions: above and below, up and down, in and out. We use positive numbers for one direction and negative numbers for the other. A negative number has a minus sign: −8 is read “negative 8.”

0 is the starting point between the two directions. It is neither positive nor negative.

SituationPositiveZero meansNegative
Temperatureabove zero: 12°F0 degreesbelow zero: −8°F
Elevationabove sea level: 300 ftsea levelbelow sea level: −40 ft
Bank accountdeposit: $25no changewithdrawal: −$25
Footballgain: 6 yardsno gain or lossloss: −6 yards
Buildingfloor 3ground floor2 floors below: −2
Electric chargepositive: 4neutralnegative: −4
Example

A diver is 15 feet below sea level. Which number represents the diver’s position?

Sea level is 0. “Below” is the negative direction.

Answer: −15 feet

Negative numbers on a number line

Positive numbers are to the right of 0. Negative numbers are to the left. To read a point, check what each tick mark counts by first.

Opposites

Two numbers are opposites when they are the same distance from 0 on different sides. 3 and −3 are opposites. The opposite of 0 is 0.

The minus sign can mean “the opposite of.” So −(−5) means the opposite of −5, which is 5. Taking the opposite twice brings you back to the number you started with.

Example

What is −(−9)?

−9 is 9 units left of 0. Its opposite is 9 units right of 0.

Answer: 9

Fractions and decimals below 0

Negative fractions and decimals sit between the negative integers. −2.5 is halfway between −3 and −2. −12 is halfway between −1 and 0.

Example

Between which two integers is −4.3?

It is a little more than 4 units left of 0, so it is past −4 but not as far as −5.

Answer: between −5 and −4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 20 for “20 feet below sea level”Below, loss, withdrawal and under par are negative: −20
Reading −2.5 as −1.5Count left from −2: −2.5 is farther from 0 than −2
Counting each tick as 1 when the scale counts by 2 or 0.5Find the tick value first: label difference ÷ spaces
Thinking −(−5) = −5The opposite of −5 is 5
Thinking the opposite of 4 is 1414 is the reciprocal. The opposite of 4 is −4
Counting tick marks instead of spaces for fractionsThirds have 3 spaces between whole numbers, not 3 tick marks

faq.q: How do you explain negative numbers to a 6th grader?
faq.a: Negative numbers describe the opposite direction from 0, like below zero on a thermometer, below sea level or money taken out of an account. On a number line they are to the left of 0.

faq.q: What does 0 mean with positive and negative numbers?
faq.a: 0 is the starting point between the two directions, and it depends on the situation: sea level for elevation, the ground floor in a building, no gain or loss in football, or a neutral electric charge.

faq.q: What is the opposite of a negative number?
faq.a: It is the positive number the same distance from 0. The opposite of −7 is 7, so −(−7) = 7.

faq.q: How do you find −2.5 on a number line?
faq.a: Go to −2, then move half a unit farther left. −2.5 is halfway between −3 and −2.

sets.title: Positive and negative numbers in real life

items.q: At 6 a.m. in Duluth, the temperature was 9 degrees below zero. By 3 p.m., it was 14 degrees above zero. Which number represents the temperature at 6 a.m.?
items.e: “Below zero” is the negative direction, so the number is −9. Here, 0 would mean 0 degrees.

items.q: A submarine is 240 feet below sea level. A helicopter flies 600 feet above sea level. Which number represents the submarine’s position?
items.e: “Below sea level” is the negative direction, so the number is −240. Here, 0 would mean sea level.

items.q: Omar’s bank account changed twice. On Monday, he made a deposit of $35. On Friday, he made a withdrawal of $20. Which number represents the Friday change to the account?
items.e: “A withdrawal” is the negative direction, so the number is −20. Here, 0 would mean no change to the account.

items.q: On the first play, the Hawks had a gain of 12 yards. On the next play, they had a loss of 7 yards. Which number represents the second play?
items.e: “A loss” is the negative direction, so the number is −7. Here, 0 would mean no gain and no loss.

items.q: In a hotel, the pool is 2 floors below ground level. The gym is 5 floors above ground level. Which number represents the floor of the pool?
items.e: “Below ground level” is the negative direction, so the number is −2. Here, 0 would mean ground level.

items.q: In a golf game, Grace finished 3 strokes over par and Kai finished 2 strokes under par. Which number represents Kai’s score compared with par?
items.e: “Under par” is the negative direction, so the number is −2. Here, 0 would mean par.

items.q: Noah’s bank account changed twice. On Monday, he made a withdrawal of $60. On Friday, he made a deposit of $45. Which number represents the Monday change to the account?
items.e: “A withdrawal” is the negative direction, so the number is −60. Here, 0 would mean no change to the account.

items.q: On the first play, the Bears had a gain of 6 yards. On the next play, they had a loss of 15 yards. Which number represents the first play?
items.e: “A gain” is the positive direction, so the number is 6. Here, 0 would mean no gain and no loss.

items.q: Elevation is measured in feet above or below sea level. What does an elevation of 0 feet mean?
c: at the bottom of the ocean
at the top of a mountain
items.e: Above sea level is positive and below sea level is negative. 0 is the starting point between them: exactly at sea level.

items.q: A thermometer shows degrees Celsius (°C). What does 0°C mean?
c: the temperature at which water freezes
the temperature at which water boils
items.e: On the Celsius scale, water freezes at 0°C. Temperatures colder than that are negative, so 0°C is not the coldest possible: water freezes at 0°C.

items.q: In football, a gain of yards is positive and a loss of yards is negative. What does a change of 0 yards mean?
c: the ball went to the other team
items.e: 0 is between gaining and losing. A change of 0 yards means the ball ended where the play started: no gain and no loss.

items.q: In an elevator, floors below the ground floor are negative. What does floor 0 mean?
c: a floor that does not exist
items.e: Floors above ground are positive and floors below are negative. 0 is the level between them: the ground floor.

items.q: An object can have a positive or a negative electric charge. What does a charge of 0 mean?
c: it has a very large charge
items.e: Positive and negative charges balance out at 0. An object with a charge of 0 is neutral.

items.q: Which situation could the number −18 represent?
items.e: A negative number shows the direction that is below or less than 0. A withdrawal of $18 matches −18. The other choices are positive.

items.q: Which situation could the number −9 represent?
items.e: A negative number shows the direction that is below or less than 0. A loss of 9 yards matches −9. The other choices are positive.

items.q: Which situation could the number −40 represent?
items.e: A negative number shows the direction that is below or less than 0. 40 feet below sea level matches −40. The other choices are positive.

items.q: Which situation could the number −5 represent?
items.e: A negative number shows the direction that is below or less than 0. 5 degrees below zero matches −5. The other choices are positive.

items.q: Which of these would be written as a negative number?
items.e: Spending $12 is the opposite of earning $12, so it is written as −12. The other three are positive.

items.q: Which of these would be written as a negative number?
items.e: 4 strokes under par is the opposite of 4 strokes over par, so it is written as −4. The other three are positive.

items.q: Which of these would be written as a negative number?
items.e: 3 floors below ground level is the opposite of 3 floors above ground level, so it is written as −3. The other three are positive.

sets.title: Read integers on a number line

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −2, so A = −3. Do not drop the minus sign: A is to the left of 0.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −4, so A = −5. Do not drop the minus sign: A is to the left of 0.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −6, so A = −7. Do not drop the minus sign: A is to the left of 0.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of 0, so A = −1. Do not drop the minus sign: A is to the left of 0.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of 6, so A = 5.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 2, and there are 2 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −8, so A = −9. Do not drop the minus sign: A is to the left of 0.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 2 tick marks to the left of −5, so A = −7.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 2 tick marks to the right of −5, so A = −3.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 2 tick marks to the right of −10, so A = −8.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −5, so A = −6.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of 5, so A = 4.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: The labels count by 5, and there are 5 spaces between labels, so each tick mark is 1. Point A is 1 tick mark to the right of −10, so A = −9.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 10, so each tick mark is 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Point A is 3 tick marks to the left of 0: −2, −4, −6. A = −6.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 25, so each tick mark is 25 ÷ 5 = 5. Point A is 3 tick marks to the left of 0: −5, −10, −15. A = −15.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 10, so each tick mark is 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Point A is 2 tick marks to the left of 0: −2, −4. A = −4.

items.q: What number is at point A?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 25, so each tick mark is 25 ÷ 5 = 5. Point A is 4 tick marks to the left of 0: −5, −10, −15, −20. A = −20.

items.q: Which point is at −5?
items.e: −5 is 5 units to the left of 0. Point B is there. The point at 5 is to the right of 0.

items.q: Which point is at −3?
items.e: −3 is 3 units to the left of 0. Point D is there. The point at 3 is to the right of 0.

items.q: Which point is at −7?
items.e: −7 is 7 units to the left of 0. Point C is there. The point at 7 is to the right of 0.

items.q: Which point is at −1?
items.e: −1 is 1 unit to the left of 0. Point A is there. The point at 1 is to the right of 0.

sets.title: Opposites and the opposite of the opposite

items.q: What is the opposite of 9?
items.e: The opposite is the same distance from 0, on the other side of 0. Change the sign: the opposite of 9 is −9. (Flipping the number to 19 gives the reciprocal, not the opposite.)

items.q: What is the opposite of −14?
items.e: The opposite is the same distance from 0, on the other side of 0. Change the sign: the opposite of −14 is 14. (Flipping the number to −114 gives the reciprocal, not the opposite.)

items.q: What is the opposite of 34?
items.e: The opposite is the same distance from 0, on the other side of 0. Change the sign: the opposite of 34 is −34. (Flipping the number to 43 gives the reciprocal, not the opposite.)

items.q: What is the opposite of −2.5?
items.e: The opposite is the same distance from 0, on the other side of 0. Change the sign: the opposite of −2.5 is 2.5. (Flipping the number to −0.4 gives the reciprocal, not the opposite.)

items.q: What is the opposite of 0?
items.e: The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0 on the other side. 0 is 0 units from itself, so the opposite of 0 is 0.

items.q: What is −(−7)?
items.e: −(−7) means “the opposite of −7.” −7 is 7 units to the left of 0, so its opposite is 7 units to the right: 7.

items.q: What is the opposite of the opposite of 11?
items.e: The opposite of 11 is −11. The opposite of that is 11 again. Taking the opposite twice brings you back: 11.

items.q: What is −(−2.5)?
items.e: −(−2.5) means “the opposite of −2.5.” −2.5 is 2.5 units to the left of 0, so its opposite is 2.5 units to the right: 2.5.

items.q: What is the opposite of the opposite of −6?
items.e: The opposite of −6 is 6. The opposite of that is −6 again. Taking the opposite twice brings you back: −6.

items.q: What is −(−(−4))?
items.e: Work from the inside: −(−4) = 4, and the opposite of 4 is −4. Three minus signs: −4.

items.q: What is the opposite of the number at point A?
items.e: Point A is at −6, 6 units from 0. The opposite is 6 units from 0 on the other side: 6.

items.q: What is the opposite of the number at point A?
items.e: Point A is at 4, 4 units from 0. The opposite is 4 units from 0 on the other side: −4.

items.q: What is the opposite of the number at point A?
items.e: Point A is at −7, 7 units from 0. The opposite is 7 units from 0 on the other side: 7.

items.q: What is the opposite of the number at point A?
items.e: Point A is at −3, 3 units from 0. The opposite is 3 units from 0 on the other side: 3.

items.q: Which point is at the opposite of −4?
items.e: The opposite of −4 is 4, 4 units to the right of 0. Point B is there. The point at −4 is the number you started from, not its opposite.

items.q: Which point is at the opposite of 5?
items.e: The opposite of 5 is −5, 5 units to the left of 0. Point C is there. The point at 5 is the number you started from, not its opposite.

items.q: Which point is at −(−3)?
items.e: −(−3) is 3, 3 units to the right of 0. Point A is there. The point at −3 is the number you started from, not its opposite.

items.q: Two numbers are opposites. On a number line, each one is 6 units from 0. What are the two numbers?
items.e: Opposites are the same distance from 0 on different sides. 6 units right of 0 is 6, and 6 units left is −6: 6 and −6. (3 and −3 are 6 units apart, but each is only 3 units from 0.)

items.q: Point A is 9 units to the left of 0. Point B is at the opposite of point A. Where is point B?
items.e: A is at −9. Its opposite is 9, the same distance from 0 on the other side: 9 units to the right of 0. (18 units is the distance from A to B, not from 0 to B.)

items.q: Which statement is true?
c: −8 and 8 are on the same side of 0
items.e: −(−8) means the opposite of −8, which is 8. −8 and 8 are on different sides of 0, each 8 units away. True: −(−8) = 8.

sets.title: Fractions and decimals on the number line

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a decimal.
items.e: There are 2 spaces between whole numbers, so each tick mark is 0.5. Point A is halfway between −3 and −2: −2.5. It is to the left of 0, so it is negative.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a decimal.
items.e: There are 2 spaces between whole numbers, so each tick mark is 0.5. Point A is halfway between −1 and 0: −0.5. It is to the left of 0, so it is negative.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a decimal.
items.e: There are 2 spaces between whole numbers, so each tick mark is 0.5. Point A is halfway between −4 and −3: −3.5. It is to the left of 0, so it is negative.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a decimal.
items.e: There are 2 spaces between whole numbers, so each tick mark is 0.5. Point A is halfway between 1 and 2: 1.5.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a decimal.
items.e: There are 4 spaces between whole numbers, so each tick mark is 0.25. Point A is 3 tick marks to the left of −1: −1.75. Each tick is 0.25, not 0.1.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a decimal.
items.e: There are 4 spaces between whole numbers, so each tick mark is 0.25. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −1: −1.25. Each tick is 0.25, not 0.1.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a decimal.
items.e: There are 10 spaces between whole numbers, so each tick mark is 0.1. Point A is 7 tick marks to the left of 0: −0.7.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a decimal.
items.e: There are 10 spaces between whole numbers, so each tick mark is 0.1. Point A is 3 tick marks to the left of −1: −1.3.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a fraction or mixed number.
items.e: Count the spaces, not the tick marks: each whole is cut into 4 equal spaces, so each tick mark is 14. Point A is 3 tick marks to the left of 0: −34.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a fraction or mixed number.
items.e: Count the spaces, not the tick marks: each whole is cut into 2 equal spaces, so each tick mark is 12. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −1: −1 12.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a fraction or mixed number.
items.e: Count the spaces, not the tick marks: each whole is cut into 4 equal spaces, so each tick mark is 14. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of −2: −2 14.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a fraction or mixed number.
items.e: Count the spaces, not the tick marks: each whole is cut into 3 equal spaces, so each tick mark is 13. Point A is 1 tick mark to the left of 0: −13.

items.q: What number is at point A? Write it as a fraction or mixed number.
items.e: Count the spaces, not the tick marks: each whole is cut into 3 equal spaces, so each tick mark is 13. Point A is 2 tick marks to the left of −1: −1 23.

items.q: Which point is at −1.5?
items.e: Each tick mark is 0.5. −1.5 is 1 tick mark to the left of −1. Point A is there.

items.q: Which point is at −12?
items.e: Each tick mark is 12. −12 is 1 tick mark to the left of 0. Point C is there.

items.q: Which point is at −2.25?
items.e: Each tick mark is 0.25. −2.25 is 1 tick mark to the left of −2. Point D is there.

items.q: Which point is at −34?
items.e: Each tick mark is 14. −34 is 3 tick marks to the left of 0. Point B is there.

items.q: Between which two integers is −3.4 on a number line?
items.e: −3.4 is a little more than 3 units to the left of 0. It is past −3 but not as far as −4: between −4 and −3.

items.q: What number is halfway between −5 and −4?
items.e: Halfway between two whole numbers is the half: between −5 and −4 is −4.5. It is negative because both numbers are to the left of 0.

items.q: Where is −2 14 on a number line?
items.e: −2 14 is 14 past −2, going left. So it is between −3 and −2, closer to −2.

items.q: On a winter morning in Fargo, Luis read the thermometer: 12 degrees below zero (°F). In the afternoon, it was 5 degrees above zero. Which number shows the morning temperature?
items.e: Below zero is negative. The morning temperature is −12°F. The afternoon temperature is 5°F.

items.q: On a winter morning in Anchorage, Sofia read the thermometer: 4 degrees below zero (°F). In the afternoon, it was 9 degrees above zero. Which number shows the morning temperature?
items.e: Below zero is negative. The morning temperature is −4°F. The afternoon temperature is 9°F.

items.q: Mount Whitney in California is 14,505 feet above sea level. Not far away, Badwater Basin in Death Valley is 282 feet below sea level. Which number represents the elevation of Badwater Basin?
items.e: Below sea level is negative, and sea level is 0. Badwater Basin is at −282 feet.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: There are 5 spaces between 0 and 10, so each tick mark is 10 ÷ 5 = 2 degrees. The red column ends 3 tick marks below 0: −2, −4, −6. The temperature is −6°F.

items.q: A diver’s depth gauge reads −35 feet. Sea level is 0. What does −35 mean?
items.e: Negative numbers are below sea level. −35 feet means 35 feet below sea level.

items.q: In a hotel, the ground floor is 0. Owen parks on the level marked “car.” Which number is that level?
items.e: The ground floor is 0. Levels below it are negative. The car is 2 levels below 0, at −1, then −2. The level is −2.

items.q: Eli’s bank account balance is −$15. What does this mean?
items.e: A balance of $0 means no money and no debt. A negative balance means money is owed: Eli owes the bank $15.

items.q: Sam deposits $40 into his account. Later he withdraws $25. Which pair of numbers shows the two changes, in order?
items.e: A deposit adds money, so it is positive: 40. A withdrawal takes money out, so it is negative: −25. 40 and −25.

items.q: On the first play, the Tigers lost 8 yards. On the second play, they gained 5 yards. Which pair of numbers shows the two plays, in order?
items.e: A loss is negative and a gain is positive: −8 for the first play and 5 for the second. −8 and 5.

items.q: One January morning, the temperatures were: Fairbanks −18°F, Bismarck −7°F, Chicago 3°F, Boston 0°F. Which city was the coldest?
items.e: The coldest temperature is the one farthest below 0. 18 degrees below zero is colder than 7 degrees below zero, so Fairbanks (−18°F) was the coldest.

items.q: A class plotted these temperatures on a number line: Duluth −2°F, Minneapolis −9°F, Detroit 4°F, Omaha −5°F. Which city’s point is farthest to the left?
items.e: Numbers to the left of 0 are negative, and the farther below 0, the farther left. −9 is 9 units left of 0, more than −5 or −2. Minneapolis is farthest left.

items.q: A shark swims at −40 feet. A sea turtle swims at −25 feet. Which animal is farther below sea level?
c: They are at the same depth.
Neither: both are above sea level.
items.e: −40 feet means 40 feet below sea level, and −25 feet means 25 feet below. 40 feet is deeper, so the shark is farther below.

items.q: In golf, par is 0. Ben finished 3 strokes under par. Ava finished 2 strokes over par. Which number shows Ava’s score?
items.e: Over par is positive and under par is negative. Ava is 2 over par: 2. (Ben’s score is −3.)

items.q: A rocket launch happens at time 0. The engines start 10 seconds before launch. 30 seconds after launch, the rocket passes the clouds. Which number shows when the engines start?
items.e: Before 0 is negative and after 0 is positive. 10 seconds before launch is −10 seconds.

items.q: A submarine is at −120 feet. A seagull flies at the opposite elevation. Where is the seagull?
items.e: The opposite of −120 is 120. 120 feet is positive, so it is 120 feet above sea level.

items.q: At noon, the temperature was 5°F. At midnight, it was the opposite of the noon temperature. What was the temperature at midnight?
items.e: The opposite of 5 is −5, the same distance from 0 on the other side. Midnight: −5°F.

items.q: A diver’s depth gauge reads 0 feet. Where is the diver?
c: at the surface of the water
at the bottom of the sea
items.e: 0 feet on a depth gauge is sea level, the line between above and below. The diver is at the surface of the water.

items.q: The price of a stock changed by $0 today. What does this mean?
c: The price did not go up or down.
items.e: A positive change means the price went up and a negative change means it went down. A change of 0 means the price did not go up or down.

items.q: A dolphin swims 20 feet below sea level. A pelican flies 15 feet above sea level. Which pair of numbers shows the dolphin, then the pelican?
items.e: Below sea level is negative and above is positive: dolphin −20, pelican 15. −20 and 15.

items.q: A balloon rubbed on hair picks up extra negative charge. Its charge is −5 units. The hair is left with the opposite charge. What is the charge of the hair?
items.e: The opposite of −5 is 5. The hair has a positive charge of 5 units.
